title: Cigarette prices to drop $30 under radical Coalition plan
text:
By NOAH SECOMB AND ALLANAH SCIBERRAS FOR AUSTRALIAN ASSOCIATED PRESS and CAITLIN POWELL - NEWS REPORTER

Published:  12:25 AEST, 3 September 2026   |  Updated:  12:39 AEST, 3 September 2026

176

View  comments

A pack of legal cigarettes would be about $30 cheaper under a Coalition policy it says would help stamp out the growing black market for illicit tobacco.

After One Nation proposed a 75 per cent cut to the tobacco excise in August, Liberal Leader Angus Taylor is now pushing for it to be slashed by 80 per cent.

The move would see a packet of cigarettes fall to prices not seen since 2013.

Taylor, who is seeking to counter a surge in popularity for Pauline Hanson's party that has also seen support for his Coalition drop to near-record lows, said he is confident making legal cigarettes competitive would undercut the illegal trade.

'I understand business, and sadly, this is a bad business that we have to destroy,' he told ABC News Breakfast on Thursday.

'We've got the worst of all worlds right now, with rising smoking, rising crime, and the result of this is that there's less tax revenue for the government.'

The current excise, which adds about $1.55 to the cost of every cigarette and pushes the average price of a legal pack of 25 over $50, has been blamed for a surge in organised criminal activity and a wave of firebombings on retailers in major cities.

An estimated 80 per cent of all tobacco consumed in 2025 was illicit, up from 12 per cent in 2017 according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Liberal Leader Angus Taylor announces a pack of legal cigarettes would be about $30 cheaper under a Coalition policy

The current excise has been blamed for a surge in organised criminal activity and a wave of firebombings on retailers in major cities

A Coalition-led inquiry, which handed down its final report on Friday, called for an immediate pause to the excise and further investigation into possible impacts of lowering taxes.

The Albanese government has resisted making any change to the excise, which reaps billions every year, despite growing pressure from economists and NSW Labor premier Chris Minns.

Senior government minister Tanya Plibersek has rubbished the Opposition's policy, labelling it a race to the bottom.

'It will kill people. Like seriously, we have some of the lowest smoking rates in the world because cigarettes are expensive,' she said on News24.

Greens senator David Shoebridge has echoed these accusations and said the Coalition policy ignores public health concerns.

Meanwhile, deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume is adamant the Coalition has not copied the homework of One Nation.

'This is not a slogan. This is not a headline. This is a solution to a policy problem, a failure of this government,' she told Channel Nine's Today.

The Coalition's policy includes $200million for law enforcement and a further $60million for a public health campaign to discourage smoking.

The announcement comes as a man is fighting for his life in hospital after being found with severe burns following a tobacco shop firebombing in Melton, outside Melbourne

Will cheaper cigarettes help fight crime, or worsen public health and addiction in Australia?

The announcement comes as a man is fighting for his life in hospital after being found with severe burns following a tobacco shop firebombing.

The person, who has not yet been identified, was discovered near The Boss tobacco store in Melton, on the outskirts of Melbourne's northwest, at 3am on Thursday.

Fire crews found the man after responding to the fire, which completely engulfed the shop. Police have deemed the blaze suspicious.

Detectives remained at the scene on Thursday, with parts of Melton's High Street closed off.

The man has been airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.

'The exact circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated,' a police spokesperson said.
